agents/index.html.9a9389d2d9: <1>Plain instructions.</1> HypGraph is a research record. Use it whenever you investigate a question with evidence and need to say what is established. Read before writing (<2/>). Write hypotheses with predictions. Write each experiment's expected outcome per hypothesis <3>before</3> running it. Record runs with hashed files. Bind every number in a claim to a result field. Never write "always/never/proves" without k of n with k = 0 or n. Never call something ruled out without a power check. Report standing exactly as the record states it. When a write is refused, fix what the message says. Short version: <4>/llms.txt</4> · full skill: <5>/SKILL.md</5>.

never/index.html.128c31cba3: "Never" is the most expensive word in research.
never/index.html.1ae2de0521: Zero failures in <1>n</1> trials doesn't mean a rate of zero. It means the rate is probably below 1 − 0.05<2>1/<3>n</3></2> — about 3/<4>n</4>. Everything built on a "never" inherits the difference, and at scale the difference is people.

never/index.html.2cb7b32acd: Red-team prompts, test cases, eval items, patients, launches — any trials where the thing could have happened. The bound is 95%: exact at zero (1 − 0.05<1>1/n</1>), Wilson otherwise.

never/index.html.4004e27d09: An orchestrator hands a question to a few agents; each hands pieces to a few more. One of them runs the trials, sees nothing, and writes <1>never</1>. Every agent above it repeats the word and drops the number it came from — that is the game. The work built on the word is the cost already paid; finding the word again when the case turns up is the cost of correcting course. Set the team and the trials; the arithmetic is the same as above.

verify/index.html.9c4f55ca1a: <1>Proves:</1> every event's hash is the SHA-256 of the exact string shown and each links to the one before; every node, version, link, withdrawal, retraction and lease in the bundle was written by an event and matches it field by field; and no row an event wrote is missing. Nothing was edited, added or dropped after it was written. The facts the explorer shows beside it (which nodes and links, their titles, authors, times, whether withdrawn) are checked against those rows too.
verify/index.html.1d1ca1608e: <1>Doesn't cover:</1> the <2>standing</2> (review state, support, at-risk, the one-line summary). That is what the exporting engine derived; re-derive it from the verified rows with <3/>. Records written before 0.7.13 didn't hash a few row fields into their events (a link's reason, say); the result lists those as <4>not covered</4>.
verify/index.html.0ac36a8b2f: <1>Doesn't trust the bundle's own policy</1> (who the importer and reviewers are): the chain doesn't cover it, so this page uses the default importer and says when the bundle names another. To check under the policy its publisher states, use <2/> (or <3/>).
verify/index.html.ec2b912378: <1>Doesn't prove on its own:</1> that the whole record wasn't rebuilt from scratch. For that, paste the <2>head</2> hash published at the time (in a paper, a preregistration, a repository tag) above.
verify/index.html.2ca5e33312: <1>Scoped bundles</1> (one investigation out of a shared record) redact the events outside it. Those can't be checked, and the result says so: that they lie outside is the bundle's word, and only the full record against the published head rules out a change hidden among them. The scope itself must name an investigation and the bundle hold only its nodes, so no claim can pose as the investigation and no whole record as one of its parts.
